Calculate windfarm-colony distances

bdy_get_distances.Rd

Calculates the shortest path distances between marine bird colonies and wind farms

Usage

bdy_get_distances(colonies, windfarms, costMatrix, doShpa = T, progress = NULL)

Arguments

colonies

sf table where each row is a colony of interest, as outputted by bdy_summarise_colonies(). Must contain the columns:

  • 'colony_code': character, unique identifiers for each colony

  • 'geometry': sf coordinates of the colony centroids

  • 'seafront': character, which sea front is the colony located in

windfarms

sf table where each row is a wind farm of interest. Must contain the columns:

  • 'NAME': character, unique identifier for each wind farm

  • 'geometry': sf coordinates of the wind farm centroid

  • 'seafront': character, which sea front is the colony located in

costMatrix

named list containing cost rasters (Transition object from package gdistance) representing the land areas as costly and marine areas as cost free, as outputted by bdy_get_cost_raster(). Must contain one object per sea front, with names identical to names in column 'facade' of argument 'colonies' and column 'Facade' of argument 'windfarms'. Used to calculate shortest path distances for strictly marine birds which do not fly over the land.

doShpa

boolean. If set to false, only the euclidean distance is calculated which makes the computation faster, especially if there are many wind farms.

progress

R shiny Progress object used to show the calculation progress to the user. Only for use within a shiny application.

Value

List containing 2 matrices with identical format (colonies as rows and wind farms as columns):
'eucl_dist' contains the euclidian distances and 'shpa_dist' contains the shortest path distances (filled with NAs if doShpa=F)

See also

bdy_get_cost_raster(),bdy_summarise_colonies()
